title: Check current secure connections via File > Connections window (test tunnel context)
summary: Use the OptiSweep application UI to open File > Connections and view the current connections shown in the bottom area/pane. The source describes these as the current “secure connections,” which can be used while troubleshooting around test tunnel checks and related startup/delayed connectivity behavior.
when_to_use: When troubleshooting connectivity issues in the context of checking the test tunnel, and you need to view the current secure connections shown by the application’s File > Connections window.
not_for: Do not use this procedure as a complete connectivity remediation step; the source only instructs how to view the secure connections and does not provide additional corrective actions if the expected connections are not shown.
roles_and_responsibilities: L1_support: Open the OptiSweep application, navigate to File > Connections, and report what the Connections window shows in the bottom area as the current secure connections.
access_or_tools_needed: OptiSweep application UI with a File menu
Connections window accessible via File > Connections

visual_references.description: Frame showing the Connections window content (Network Connections / current connections list) referenced by the source while describing “secure connections.”

steps.title: Open the relevant application and navigate to File > Connections
steps.purpose: Access the window that displays the current connections described by the source as secure connections.
steps.instruction: In the OptiSweep application, use the File menu and click Connections to open the Connections window.
steps.healthy_condition: The Connections window is visible and ready to display the current connections list in its bottom area/pane.
steps.failure_condition: The Connections window does not open (or cannot be accessed via File > Connections).

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: Transcript: "Check your test tunnel. You can under file click connections. It'll pop up on the bottom the current connections."

steps.title: Look at the bottom area where the source says it shows the current connections
steps.purpose: Identify the specific area of the Connections window that contains the current connections list.
steps.instruction: In the Connections window, check the bottom area/pane where the current connections are shown.
steps.expected_result: The bottom area/pane shows a list of current connections.
steps.healthy_condition: A current connections list is visible in the bottom area/pane of the Connections window.
steps.failure_condition: The Connections window does not show a current connections list in the bottom area/pane.

actions.label: Inspect bottom connections list
actions.exact_action: View the bottom area/pane of the Connections window showing current connections

stop_or_escalate_if: If the Connections window does not show current secure connections (i.e., no current connections list in the bottom area/pane), stop and escalate because the source provides no additional troubleshooting steps.
